newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Jan 23.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - The FTSE 100 index finished at a record high for the fifth time this year, lifted by weaker sterling and a growing belief that British base rates would remain steady for the foreseeable future. The FTSE 100 closed 52.4 higher at 4,271.5.

FRANKFURT - Germany's DAX index ended bourse trade slightly higher in range-trade dealings, recovering from earlier weakness after news that German M3 money supply growth was higher than expected in December. The 30-share index ended up 4.79 points at 3,033.46 points after spending the session within a 20-point range, helped in part by the ongoing strength in the dollar and on Wall Street. The DAX later ended the IBIS computer trading session at 3,037.28 points.

PARIS - Shares rose 0.77 percent to a fresh record close -- the sixth this year -- with financial stocks blazing the trail. Shares in banks Societe Generale and Credit Commercial de France (CCF) led the rally. Other blue chips in the long-suffering sector advanced, sweeping the CAC index to all-time highs, traders said. The bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 18.79 points at 2,461.25.

ZURICH - Shares extended recent gains, with the Swiss Market Index ending one percent higher at a record in heavy volume as index heavyweight Roche climbed farther and banks saw a resurgence of interest. The blue-chip SMI rose 45.5 points to 4,160.8 after hitting an all-time high at 4,163.5. The all-share Swiss Performance Index added 21.7 points to 2,660.37.

TOKYO - Stocks ended on a somewhat feeble note, following a surge of over 3.5 percent on the previous day, as there were few factors to sustain the rise, brokers said. Eyes were glued to the weak yen, with speculation on what could happen should it weakened further. The Nikkei 225 was 104.42 points or 0.58 percent lower at 17,909.46.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed moderately lower in cautious trading, pulled down by profit-taking in the market leaders, particularly property stocks. The Hang Seng Index closed 82.46 points lower at 13,610.33, slightly above the day's low of 13,591.35. Turnover was HK$8.28 billion, well off Wednesday's HK$11.16 billion.

SYDNEY - Shares ended just one point up with weaker resources counteracted by a buoyant banking sector which was inspired by sector leader National Australia Bank after it reported strong first quarter earnings. The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed one point firmer at 2,434.5.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended weak as poor sentiment from the gold price knocked prices in quiet trade. Some profit-taking also hit industrial shares after institutions had been investing new money since the beginning of the month. The gold index dropped 24.8 points to a fresh one year low of 1,353.2. The industrial index lost 63.5 points to 8,083.1 and together they dragged down the overall index 38.9 points to 6,717.9.
